# Vertical overlay: Food and Agriculture

**Level:** CISA critical infrastructure sector (child of NAICS 11 Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 311612 Meat Processed from Carcasses. Meat processing plant with automated processing lines and cold-chain monitoring.
**Primary system:** Plant production and cold-chain monitoring system

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
SRMA: Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Department of Health and Human Services (HHS/FDA); FDA Food Defense program; USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (meat, poultry, egg products)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**FSMA Intentional Adulteration rule (food defense)**, 21 CFR Part 121. The only binding, sector-specific federal security rule for food facilities; its vulnerability-assessment/mitigation structure maps well to cyber-physical risks (e.g., tampering via compromised batching/dosing controls). Pair with NIST CSF 2.0 for IT/OT control coverage since Part 121 is not IT-specific.
Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/part-121

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Food defense plans / vulnerability assessments; Recipes, formulations and trade secrets; Supplier and traceability records (FSMA 204); Consumer PII and payment card data; Protected Critical Infrastructure Information (PCII) if submitted to DHS
- **Critical systems:** Batch/recipe control systems (DCS/PLC); Cold-chain and refrigeration controls (ammonia systems); MES and ERP; Warehouse management systems; Traceability/lot-coding systems; Packaging line automation
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Ransomware halting processing lines and cold-chain monitoring
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** AI quality inspection on processing lines

## Notes
CFATS formerly covered ammonia/chemical holdings at some food facilities but authority lapsed July 2023 (see c-chemical). MTSA/USCG cyber rule applies only to waterfront facilities with MTSA security plans (e.g., grain elevators on navigable waters).
